newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa alliances will boost 97 profits.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa alliances will boost 97 profits.

text.p: A cooperative alliance with the Scandinavian airline SAS will improve net earnings by 100 million marks ($65 million) in 1997, German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said in a statement on Monday.
Management board chairman Juergen Weber said that Lufthansa's code-sharing agreement with SAA South African Airways would boost net earnings by 10 to 20 million marks in the coming year.

Lufthansa's co-operative alliance with Thai Airways contributed between 20 and 30 million to group profits in 1996, while its agreement with United Airlines in the United States had boosted profits up 100 million marks, Weber said.

A code-sharing agreement with Brazil's Varig brought in 20 million marks. Weber said in July that Lufthansa was expecting hundreds of millions of marks in extra income from its international co-operative alliances. ($1=1.5312 Mark)
